correctness.rationale: Direct computation on all four matrix units produces the 4x4 normalized Choi matrix. Comparison of its two block determinants, and those after partial transpose, rigorously yields the CP and EB inequalities. Their exponential ratios are strictly decreasing, establishing the unique thresholds; asymptotic Taylor expansion and the alpha=1+u/log(1/s) substitution yield the fixed-alpha fractional-power gap and logarithmic crossover. Pure-beta and alpha=0 boundaries are separately checked. Reproducible independent numerical construction and high-precision root tests completed 2,230 finite assertions; these tests corroborate but are not the infinite-time proof.

value.rationale: The 2026 semigroup model was introduced specifically to study restricted-positivity/non-GKSL open-system evolution. How long one waits until an arbitrary-input channel becomes CP, and for how long it can still transmit quantum entanglement, are operationally motivated, quantifiable gaps beyond the source generator classification. The sharp near-pure target law makes that transmission window collapse with a noninteger parameter-dependent exponent, while a fine \(\alpha-1=O(1/\log(1/s))\) transition reveals a distinct nonzero profile. This is a structural timescale classification, not a bare Choi positivity test or small numerical improvement; broad eventual EB existence remains established prior art.
